# Results — Study 525 (R-And-D-Intensity)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The **Chan-Lakonishok-Sougiannis R&D
premium**: rank a fixed large-cap field each month by **R&D-to-market-cap** (R&D / ME — R&D scaled
by market value, the CLS *mispricing* signal), go **long the most-intensive tertile / short the
least-intensive**, rebalance monthly with a one-year reporting lag and one execution lag, and race
the spread against SPY, against a label-shuffle placebo, and against the **R&D/sales** signal (the
pure spending-intensity cousin of [study 400](../400-patent-intensity/)). We split the claim three
ways: is the spread **statistically real** (HAC `t ≥ 2` **and** placebo survival), is it
**tradable** net of monthly turnover + short-borrow, and does **R&D/ME beat R&D/sales** as CLS
predict? Offline & deterministic from the cache; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every
number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Fundamentals tape | **SEC EDGAR** companyfacts — annual `ResearchAndDevelopmentExpense`, revenue, shares-outstanding (10-K full-year facts only; public, no key) |
| Price / return tape | yfinance monthly **total return** + auto-adjusted close (for the market-cap denominator; public, no key) |
| Window | **2005-02 → 2026-05** (256 return months; long-short over **220** holding months after the lag; **21.3** years) |
| Field | **40** long-listed large-caps spanning the R&D spectrum; **24** carry an EDGAR R&D series (the 16 R&D-light banks/staples/energy are floored to 0 — economically correct) |
| Signal | **R&D / market-cap** (CLS), formed monthly: R&D(FY Y-1) ÷ [price(month) × shares(FY Y-1)] |
| Formation / costs | **monthly** rebalance, **1-yr reporting lag** on fundamentals + **1-month execution lag** (signal at month *t* selects the book entered next month); 10 bps one-way turnover + **100 bps/yr borrow** on the short leg |
| Panel fingerprint | `8d048dab164a` |

> **Scope caveats (named on the Signal axis).** *Survivorship* — the basket is **current-membership
> projected back** to 2005 (delisted names absent). Its direction is reasoned about in writing:
> **both** the long leg (R&D-heavy tech/pharma) **and** the short leg (R&D-light banks/staples/
> energy) are survivors, so the survivorship tilt is largely **common to both legs** of the
> long/short rather than a clean push on the spread. *Value cousin* — because the denominator is
> market value, R&D/ME mechanically tilts toward *cheap* stocks, so it overlaps the book-to-market
> value factor; a positive spread is partly a relabelled value/growth tilt. *One field* — 40 names
> is a transparent slice, not the CRSP universe; the verdict is about *whether the audited R&D/ME
> tilt clears the bar on a clean tape*.

The long (high R&D/ME) and short (low R&D/ME) tertiles as of the final-month signal:

- **Long (high R&D / market-cap):** ADBE, AMGN, BMY, CSCO, DE, GILD, IBM, INTC, LLY, MRK, ORCL, PFE, QCOM
- **Short (low R&D / market-cap):** AXP, DUK, GS, HD, JPM, KO, LOW, MCD, T, USB, VZ, WFC, WMT

Semis, software and pharma on the long side; banks, staples, retail, utilities and telco on the
short side — the same sector map study 400 found, and the first clue the spread overlaps a
**style/value** axis rather than a pure "innovation" axis.

## The race — high-R&D/ME long, low-R&D/ME short, vs the market

Equal-weight, monthly rebalanced; CAGR / annualised Sharpe / max drawdown over the 220 holding months.

| book | CAGR | Sharpe | max drawdown | mean (ann) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Long — high R&D/ME (top tertile)** | **16.90%** | 1.06 | −39.6% | +16.99% |
| Short leg — low R&D/ME (bottom tertile) | 11.77% | 0.80 | −38.7% | +12.38% |
| **Long − short (the R&D/ME spread)** | 3.92% | **0.37** | −26.3% | **+4.61%** |
| S&P 500 (SPY) | 11.11% | 0.78 | −50.8% | +11.70% |

The long leg out-earns both the short leg and the market — the directional claim is *not nothing*.
But the long-short Sharpe is **0.37**: a thin, noisy spread, not a crisp factor.

## The Signal-axis test — HAC t-stats

Newey-West HAC t of the monthly spread (the desk's `REAL` needs `t ≥ 2` **and** placebo survival):

| spread | mean | HAC t | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **Long − short (R&D/ME spread)** | **+4.61%/yr** | **1.69** | 220 |
| Long − SPY | +4.56%/yr | **2.52** | 220 |
| Short − SPY | −0.05%/yr | −0.02 | 220 |

The R&D/ME long-short is **+4.61%/yr but `t = 1.69` — it does not clear the `t ≥ 2` bar.** The
edge is **entirely the long leg**: long-minus-SPY clears 2 (t = 2.52) while the short leg is
*indistinguishable from the market* (t = −0.02). So there is no two-sided premium — the high-R&D/ME
names beat the market, the low-R&D/ME names *are* the market, and the long-short spread is the
long-only edge minus nothing. A long-only growth/value tilt, not a clean cross-sectional factor.

## Placebo — does the *signal* do the work, or any split? (it survives)

Permute the signal labels across names (same per-name R&D/ME values, wrong names) and rebuild the
long-short, 400 draws:

| | annualised long-short spread |
|---|--:|
| **R&D/ME long-short (this study)** | **+4.61%/yr** |
| Shuffled-label null — mean | +0.41%/yr |
| Shuffled-label null — std dev | 1.84%/yr |
| **R&D/ME percentile in the null** | **99.8** |
| **Placebo two-sided p** | **0.005** |

This is the honest two-sidedness. A *shuffled* signal pays ≈0%/yr (as it should — no information),
so the R&D/ME spread of +4.61%/yr is **not** a generic artefact: the ranking really does load on a
persistent cross-sectional axis (99.8th percentile, **p = 0.005**). **But** that axis is the
growth/value style tilt (the long names *are* cheap-intangibles tech/pharma; the short names *are*
banks/staples/retail), and the spread's *own time series* still fails `t ≥ 2`. So the signal
survives the placebo (it is real-as-an-axis) yet fails the HAC bar (its return is inside its own
error bar): the textbook `WEAK` pattern — a real tilt whose return is unproven.

## The CLS denominator contrast — R&D/ME vs R&D/sales (the third axis)

CLS's decisive claim is that scaling R&D by **market value** predicts returns where scaling by
**sales** does not. We race the two on the same basket:

| signal | long-short | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|
| **R&D / market-cap** (CLS mispricing signal) | **+4.61%/yr** | **1.69** |
| R&D / sales (spending intensity — study 400) | +3.99%/yr | 1.40 |

**R&D/ME *does* beat R&D/sales** — higher spread (+4.61% vs +3.99%) and higher *t* (1.69 vs 1.40),
exactly the CLS ordering: scaling by price (cheapness) is the better signal. The denominator
prediction is **confirmed in direction**. But the win is *thin* — both signals fail `t ≥ 2`, and
the gap between them (≈0.6%/yr) is far inside the noise — so it confirms CLS's *ranking* of the two
signals without rescuing either to significance on this tape.

## Robustness — long/short fraction

Tighten the sort from halves to quintiles:

| split | long-short | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|
| top/bottom **half** | +3.97%/yr | 1.70 |
| top/bottom **tertile** (headline) | +4.61%/yr | 1.69 |
| top/bottom **quartile** | +5.66%/yr | 1.87 |
| top/bottom **quintile** | +6.86%/yr | **2.24** |

Here the spread *strengthens* as you concentrate (unlike study 400's R&D/sales, which weakened) —
it reaches `t = 2.24` at the tightest, **8-name-per-leg quintile**. That is a *better* signature
than the sales signal, but it clears 2 **only** at the most concentrated, least-diversified split
(where a handful of names drive the result and idiosyncratic risk is highest), not at the tradable
tertile. A signal significant only at the extreme tail of the sort, fragile to costs (below), reads
`WEAK`, not `REAL`.

## Costs + short-borrow — the thin edge leaks

| | gross | net (10 bps turnover + 100 bps/yr borrow on the short) |
|---|--:|--:|
| **Long-short spread** | **+4.61%/yr (t = 1.69)** | **+3.59%/yr (t = 1.32)** |

Monthly turnover is modest (avg ~1.6% one-way/month — the market-cap denominator only nudges the
ranking month to month), so turnover cost is small. But a long/short **pays borrow to be short** —
and a 100 bps/yr borrow fee knocks the already-insignificant +4.61%/yr spread down to **+3.59%/yr
at t = 1.32**. You cannot allocate to a long/short whose net spread is statistically
indistinguishable from zero. (The deployable object is the long-only leg, +4.56%/yr vs SPY at
t = 2.52 — but that is a value/growth tilt a style ETF gives you cheaper.)

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful, the tape is just weak

A deterministic monthly panel (fixed seed, 18 years × 40 names) where the first half are
persistently high-R&D/ME, the market beta is common to both legs, and a knob `edge` plants the
*true* annual long-high-minus-short-low premium:

| planted edge | recovered long-short spread | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|
| **`edge = 0.00`** (no true premium) | −0.43%/yr | **−0.16** |
| **`edge = 0.06`** (large +6%/yr premium) | +5.57%/yr | **+2.01** |

With **no** planted premium the long-short is flat and **insignificant** (t = −0.16 — the harness
does not manufacture a false positive). Only a **large** planted premium (+6%/yr) drives the
recovered spread to `t ≈ 2`. The engine is unbiased — it finds a premium **only** where one is
planted — so the real-tape `t = 1.69` reads as *"a real-but-small edge seen through a 21-year
keyhole,"* not a hidden bug.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The R&D/ME long-short is positive (**+4.61%/yr**), loads on a genuine
  cross-sectional axis (placebo **p = 0.005**, 99.8th percentile), and the literature reports a CLS
  R&D-valuation premium. But on this clean 21-year tape it **fails `t ≥ 2`** (HAC **t = 1.69**),
  clears 2 *only* at the most-concentrated quintile (2.24), and the edge is entirely the long leg
  (the short leg matches the market, t = −0.02). Literature + placebo survival + a
  positive-but-insignificant headline estimate ⇒ **WEAK**, not `REAL`.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Turnover cost is small, but the long/short **pays short-borrow**, which
  drops the spread to **+3.59%/yr at t = 1.32** — a net edge indistinguishable from zero. The only
  deployable object is a long-only value/growth tilt (+4.56%/yr vs SPY, t = 2.52) that a style ETF
  delivers more cheaply.
- **Does R&D/ME beat R&D/sales? — CONFIRMED (directionally).** Scaling R&D by **market value** does
  out-rank scaling by **sales** (+4.61%/yr at t = 1.69 vs +3.99%/yr at t = 1.40), exactly as
  Chan-Lakonishok-Sougiannis predict — the price denominator is the better signal. But the win is
  *thin* (≈0.6%/yr, both below `t = 2`), so CLS's *ordering* of the two signals holds while neither
  reaches significance on this survivor basket.

> **One-line.** Sort large-caps monthly by R&D-to-market-cap and the high-R&D/ME tertile beats the
> low-R&D/ME tertile by +4.61%/yr — the signal survives a label-shuffle placebo (p = 0.005) and,
> as Chan-Lakonishok-Sougiannis predict, *does* edge out the R&D/sales version — but at HAC
> **t = 1.69** the spread never clears the significance bar (only the most-concentrated quintile
> reaches t = 2.24), the whole edge is the long leg (the short leg is just the market), and
> short-borrow drags the net spread to t = 1.32: a real value/growth tilt wearing an R&D costume,
> not a distinct, tradable innovation alpha.
